title: Arabian & Damiano's Mates
subtitle: Corner kills — including the famous double rook sacrifice.
goals: Convert the g6 pawn wedge into mate

steps.say: Pedro Damiano published this attack in 1512 — and it still wins games every single day. The ingredients: a pawn wedged on g6, a rook on the open h-file, and a queen ready to swing. The recipe: sacrifice EVERYTHING that stands between your queen and h7.

steps.prompt: The h-file is open and the g6 wedge is in place. Start the demolition — the rook goes first!
hints: The rook's job is to drag the king onto h8 so the queen arrives with check.
Rh8+! The king must take (your knight covers g7) — then the queen follows with tempo.

line.say: The decoy sac — and the king cannot decline: g7 is covered by your knight.
The queen swings in with check — this is why the rook had to die: it BOUGHT this tempo.
Damiano's mate. The g6 pawn guards the queen, the f8 rook blocks the last exit. A rook down and completely winning — the sacrifice was arithmetic, not bravery.

rejections.say: The right idea one move too soon — Black slams the door with ...Rh8-trades or ...f5 counterplay. The rook sacrifice FIRST forces the king onto the fatal square with check. Order is everything.

steps.wrongSay: Think forcing: which sacrifice drags the king onto the square where your queen checks?
steps.successSay: Sac to open, check to arrive, wedge to mate — the Damiano formula.

steps.prompt: Now the FULL classic from 1512: this time the king can step back off h8 — so you'll need to sacrifice BOTH rooks!
hints: After the first Rh8+ Kxh8, your second rook takes over the h-file with check — repeat the trick!
Rh8+, Rh1+, Rh8+ again — three sacrificial checks in a row, then the queen mops up via h5 and h7.

line.say: ...and rook number two inherits the file — check!
The SECOND full rook goes into the furnace. Material is a tool, not a treasure.
Both rooks are gone — and the queen arrives exactly on time.
CHECKMATE — two whole rooks down. Damiano wrote this down in 1512; you just played all nine moves of it. The h-file was worth more than everything you gave for it.

rejections.say: Without the rook decoys, the king isn't ON h8 yet — Black defends with ...f5 or trades on h1. The sacrifices don't just open lines: they force the king to stand exactly where each check needs him.

steps.wrongSay: Nine forced moves. Every white move is a check. Start with the nearest rook.
steps.successSay: A double rook sacrifice from the year 1512 — you now share a combination with five centuries of attackers.

steps.prompt: Change of corner furniture: knight on f6, rook on the h-file. The ARABIAN mate — finish it.
hints: The f6 knight is the hero: count which squares near the king it controls.
It guards g8 AND h7 — so your rook can land on h7 untouchably.

line.say: The Arabian mate — found in Arabic chess manuscripts over a thousand years old, and still the standard finish of every h-file attack where a knight reaches f6. The oldest pattern in the book, still undefeated.

steps.wrongSay: The rook wants h7 — work out why the king can't simply take it.
steps.successSay: Knight f6 + rook on the 7th/h-file = Arabian. When your knight lands on f6 in a real game, this mate is what it's threatening.
